bug_description.normalized: In util-linux's ISO9660 probe, the staged 35663-byte witness contains a primary volume descriptor at file offset 0x8000 and a Joliet supplementary descriptor at 0x8800. The primary descriptor's 128-byte `volume_set_id` at 0x80be is a space followed by 127 underscores, and the Joliet `volume_set_id` at 0x88be survives the `%/E` escape-sequence check and contains one valid UTF16BE surrogate pair `db db dd db`. `probe_iso9660()` allocates `unsigned char buf[256]` and calls `merge_utf16be_ascii(buf, joliet->volume_set_id, pvd->volume_set_id, sizeof(pvd->volume_set_id))`, binding the helper's `len` parameter to 128 for that invocation. Because the helper's first loop consumes all 128 UTF16 bytes in 63 iterations, only 63 of the 128 ASCII bytes are consumed and 65 ASCII bytes remain for the second loop. That loop checks only `a < len`, not whether `o` still fits in `buf`, so the 65th append writes `out[256] = 0x00` at line 199. AddressSanitizer reports a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 in `merge_utf16be_ascii` and identifies `buf` in `probe_iso9660` as the overflowed stack object.

source.code: blkid_probe_get_buffer(pr, off, max(sizeof(struct boot_record), sizeof(struct iso_volume_descriptor)))
source.description: First project-code read on the vulnerable path: `probe_iso9660()` fetches the attacker-controlled ISO descriptor sector into `desc`, which the next branches reinterpret as the primary and Joliet volume descriptors.
source.value_from: The staged harness writes the exact 35663-byte witness `gt_results/arvo_53149/poc` (sha256 `eb96bbcbbcd79c55588d5e450ec901d081eab1e70be2bd0f0150cbe7983e3785`) to a temp file and calls `blkid_do_safeprobe(pr)` (`libblkid/src/fuzz.c:15-24`). During the vulnerable path, `probe_iso9660()` reads 2048-byte descriptors from offsets `0x8000` and `0x8800`; those sectors contain the primary descriptor and the `%/E` Joliet supplementary descriptor whose `volume_set_id` fields later drive the overflow.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The overflow-driving values at this call site are the paired 128-byte `volume_set_id` fields plus the fourth argument `sizeof(pvd->volume_set_id)`, which binds `merge_utf16be_ascii()`'s parameter `len` to 128 for this invocation. The caller local `len` is assigned only after the helper returns. In the witness, `pvd->volume_set_id` at file offset `0x80be` is `0x20` followed by 127 underscores, while `joliet->volume_set_id` at `0x88be` contains one valid surrogate pair `db db dd db`, which makes the helper attempt a 258-byte merge into `buf[256]`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. On the 65th ASCII-suffix append in the second loop, `o == 256`, so this write stores one byte at `buf[256]`, just past the 256-byte stack buffer `buf[0..255]` allocated in `probe_iso9660()`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `merge_utf16be_ascii /src/util-linux/libblkid/src/superblocks/iso9660.c:199:10` and identifies `buf` at line 212 as the overflowed stack object.

root_cause.description: The second loop appends remaining ASCII bytes while checking only `a < len`; it has no `out_len` parameter and no comparison between `o` and the actual 256-byte destination buffer supplied by `probe_iso9660()`.
root_cause.note: For the witnessed `volume_set_id`, the first loop ends with `a = 63`, `u = 128`, and `o = 128`, leaving 65 ASCII bytes to append. The patch fixes this obligation by adding `size_t out_len` and `o + 1 < out_len` guards before both write loops.

parser_admitted.description: The descriptor at offset `0x8800` has `vd_type == ISO_VD_SUPPLEMENTARY` and escape sequence `%/E`, so `probe_iso9660()` accepts it as a Joliet descriptor and leaves `joliet` non-null. That makes the later `if (joliet && ...)` `volume_set_id` merge branch reachable.

fine_trace.note: Pre-existing local state. This fixed-size stack buffer is declared at function entry before descriptor parsing and later becomes the destination for the 128-byte `volume_set_id` merge. ASan identifies this exact object at line 212 as the overflowed variable, with valid indices only through `buf[255]`.

fine_trace.code: unsigned char *desc = blkid_probe_get_buffer(pr, off, max(sizeof(struct boot_record), sizeof(struct iso_volume_descriptor)));
fine_trace.note: Source. In the witness loop iterations at offsets `0x8000` and `0x8800`, this call materializes the attacker-controlled volume descriptor sectors as `desc` for the later primary and Joliet descriptor aliases.

fine_trace.code:
else if (!pvd && desc[0] == ISO_VD_PRIMARY)
	pvd = (struct iso_volume_descriptor *)desc;
fine_trace.note: When the descriptor loaded from `0x8000` has `vd_type == ISO_VD_PRIMARY`, `pvd` aliases the primary volume descriptor. Its `volume_set_id` field now points at the 128-byte ASCII input later used as `ascii`, which in the witness is one space byte followed by 127 underscores.

When the descriptor loaded from `0x8800` has `vd_type == ISO_VD_SUPPLEMENTARY`, the branch aliases it as `joliet`. The witness escape sequence is `%/E`, so the `memcmp(...) != 0` conjunction is false and `joliet` stays non-null; its `volume_set_id` field now points at the 128-byte UTF16BE input later used as `utf16`, including bytes `db db dd db` at offsets 60..63 of the field.

This call selects the 128-byte `volume_set_id` fields as the merge inputs and passes `buf` as the destination with no accompanying extent argument. Because `joliet` is non-null in the witness, the invocation binds `merge_utf16be_ascii()`'s parameter `len` to `sizeof(pvd->volume_set_id) == 128`; the caller local `len` is assigned only after the helper returns.

depends_on.via: joliet remains non-null after the `%/E` check

fine_trace.note: At UTF16 byte offsets 60..63 of the witness field, bytes `db db dd db` satisfy the surrogate-pair test, so one loop iteration consumes four UTF16 bytes while incrementing `a` only once. Because almost the entire primary `volume_set_id` is `_`, the underscore arm keeps copying those UTF16 bytes instead of rejecting them. Across the full 128-byte field, the first loop finishes with `u = 128`, `a = 63`, and `o = 128`: all UTF16 input is exhausted, but 65 ASCII bytes remain to append.

depends_on.via: joliet->volume_set_id, pvd->volume_set_id, callee len from sizeof(pvd->volume_set_id)

fine_trace.note: Root cause. The second loop starts with `a = 63 < len = 128`, so it will append the 65 remaining ASCII bytes as UTF16BE `0x00` + `ascii[a]`. The loop condition checks only `a < len`; it never compares `o` against the caller's 256-byte `buf` or any `out_len`, so the loop continues even after `o` reaches the end of that stack buffer.

Sink. After 64 safe second-loop appends, the 65th append begins with `o = 256` and `a = 127`. This store therefore writes the first byte of the final UTF16BE underscore to `buf[256]`, one byte past the last valid stack slot `buf[255]`, which matches the saved ASan `stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 1` at this line.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_53149 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged ISO image to `/out/test_blkid_fuzz` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 1` in `merge_utf16be_ascii` with stack `probe_iso9660 -> superblocks_probe`.

format.name: ISO9660 image with a primary descriptor and a `%/E` Joliet supplementary descriptor
format.contract: Exactly the 35663-byte witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_53149/poc` (sha256 `eb96bbcbbcd79c55588d5e450ec901d081eab1e70be2bd0f0150cbe7983e3785`). At file offset `0x8000` it contains a primary volume descriptor whose 128-byte `volume_set_id` at `0x80be` is `0x20` followed by 127 underscore bytes (`0x5f`). At offset `0x8800` it contains a Joliet supplementary descriptor with escape sequence `%/E`; its 128-byte UTF16BE `volume_set_id` at `0x88be` includes one valid surrogate pair `db db dd db` at field-relative offsets 60..63. Those exact witness properties make `probe_iso9660()` take the `joliet` `volume_set_id` merge path, cause `merge_utf16be_ascii()` to exhaust the 128 UTF16 bytes after only 63 ASCII iterations, leave 65 ASCII bytes for the second loop, and require 258 output bytes from a 256-byte stack buffer. This contract is limited to the staged witness layout and observed path, not all ISO9660/Joliet images or all surrogate-pair labels.
